title: POC Weekly Sync - Model Selection & Version Pinning
summary: Weekly POC sync to review results from model variants and discuss version pinning strategy. Customer prefers predictable latency and deterministic rollbacks; Redwood team recommends pinning to a quantized variant for cost and using a fallback policy to a smaller model. Agreed next steps: run a 2k-token latency benchmark on dedicated pool, share pinned-model config and rollback playbook, schedule security deep-dive next week.
next_steps: Priya to run end-to-end 2k-token latency/throughput run on dedicated pool and share raw logs by 2025-06-27
Alex to send pinned-model config (JSON) + recommended rollout policy and rollback playbook by 2025-06-25
Customer to review tokenization edge-cases and share 5 representative prompts by 2025-06-26
Schedule security deep-dive (SOC2 + KMS) for week of 2025-06-30
action_items: Priya Nair: run 2k-token latency test on dedicated pool, include cold vs warm KV cache numbers; due 2025-06-27
Alex Chen: share pinned model config and sample canary rollout policy + rollback steps; due 2025-06-25
Samir Patel: collect 5 corner-case prompts and tokenization samples; due 2025-06-26
Lisa Gomez: confirm VPC peering window and provide list of required IPs; due 2025-06-29
Alex Chen: add security docs link and sample SLA language to CRM record; due 2025-06-24
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, uh this is the weekly sync for the Verity POC. we have Priya from the SE team. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Rachel Kim: good thanks Alex, quick day for us, excited to see the numbers.
[00:12] Samir Patel: hey all, morning — we've been running the two variants overnight, some initial notes in the spreadsheet.
[00:18] Priya Nair: great, so agenda — quick recap of what we ran, latency and cost numbers, discuss pinning strategy for the pilot, and next steps.
[00:27] Lisa Gomez: sounds good. shout if you need infra context, I'll chime in.
[00:31] Alex Chen: ok Priya take it away.
[00:34] Priya Nair: sure. so we compared redwood-instruct-v2 (float32 baseline) and redwood-2.1-quant (4-bit quantized) on the dedicated GPU pool you spun up. tests included 512 and 2048 token contexts, mixed prompt sizes to reflect your real traffic.
[00:48] Priya Nair: headline — redwood-2.1-quant gives ~1.9x token throughput and around 40% cost reduction on our estimator, latency tail is slightly higher on cold starts but warm runs are comparable.
[01:03] Samir Patel: can you quantify "tail"? that's what worries us most for SLAs.
[01:07] Priya Nair: sure, 95th percentile for 2k tokens was ~820ms on quantized warm runs versus 720ms on baseline float, cold start differences were up to 1.4x depending on cache hit. we did see some KV cache warmup effects.
[01:22] Alex Chen: so tradeoff is cost vs predictable tight latency. if you need hard 500ms 95th, quant might not be right, but if 800–900ms is OK we save quite a bit.
[01:34] Rachel Kim: our product requirement is <750ms 95th for interactive triage. 820ms is a little high. could we do pin to baseline for canary and fallback to quant? or the inverse?
[01:46] Priya Nair: yes you can pin a version per route. recommended pattern: pin production route to redwood-instruct-v2 (baseline) for strict latency, then configure an automatic fallback to redwood-2.1-quant during overloads or cost-traffic windows. that's what Redwood's routing policy supports.
[02:01] Samir Patel: is there an easy way to rollback to a previous model if the new pinned version causes regressions?
[02:05] Priya Nair: yes, our rollout tool supports canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% stages and automatic rollback if quality metrics dip. we can also pin to a "compat" variant. note, sometimes the model naming in the catalog is slightly different in the UI vs API — transcription sorry, naming may show as rw-instruct or redwood-instruct-v2, little inconsistencies.
[02:24] Lisa Gomez: that's ok — just want reproducible API config. can you provide the exact model id we should pin?
[02:30] Alex Chen: we'll send the pinned model config with exact model_id and checksum. Alex: action — send JSON.
[02:36] Priya Nair: also important — tokenization edge-cases. we found a few prompts where tokenization changed effective length by 10–15%, which affects batching and latency. Samir, you said you'd share sample prompts?
[02:48] Samir Patel: yes I'll drop 5 representative corner-case prompts into the shared sheet.
[02:51] Rachel Kim: about fallback, what's the policy for KV cache compatibility? we can't warm up caches if we jump between model families.
[02:59] Priya Nair: correct — KV cache isn't portable across model families/architectures. fallback to a smaller variant within same model family is ideal, because KV cache can be reused. if you must switch families, you will incur cache misses and cold-tail impacts. we documented a "graceful degrade" pattern in the playbook.
[03:15] Lisa Gomez: ok that's a constraint. suggests we prefer same-family fallbacks.
[03:19] Alex Chen: noted. Priya, can you include the fallback playbook in the config doc?
[03:23] Priya Nair: yes will attach.
[03:25] Samir Patel: on benchmarks — the dedicated pool we used was the dded-8g-rt (example name), do the numbers change much on shared hosted?
[03:33] Priya Nair: on hosted API you get variability in tail due to multitenancy, but our hosted offering has autoscaling; Dedicated is more predictable. For strict SLOs we recommend dedicated or private. also quant gains may differ depending on kernel selection on host GPU.
[03:49] Rachel Kim: can you remind us about encryption and key management? our security team wants KMS with HSM option.
[03:55] Alex Chen: yes Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs; Dedicated supports KMS integrations too. we'll share the security docs and SOC2 attestation.
[04:05] Lisa Gomez: please include network egress IPs and the VPC peering checklist.
[04:09] Alex Chen: will do.
[04:11] Priya Nair: a couple of notes from the perf runs — batching settings matter a lot. we used continuous batching with 64 token batch sizes for the 2k tests; reducing max batch reduces tail but increases cost. also quantized kernels require a slightly different micro-batch tuning.
[04:25] Samir Patel: do you have recommended starting config for our traffic profile?
[04:28] Priya Nair: yes we'll include recommended batching, max latency SLO, and suggested autoscale thresholds in the doc we send.
[04:35] Rachel Kim: any immediate red flags from the tests? model regressions, hallucination?
[04:40] Priya Nair: no major quality regressions observed in our eval prompts. small style shifts between floating and quant variants — we flagged them in the eval sheet. quality monitoring hooks can alert on LLM-eval scores and per-prompt regression.
[04:52] Lisa Gomez: what's the suggested canary cadence? we prefer faster rollouts but safe.
[04:57] Alex Chen: start with a 10% canary for 24–48 hours, monitor perf and quality, then ramp. Priya: we have a sample canary policy.
[05:04] Priya Nair: yes, I'll attach with thresholds.
[05:06] Samir Patel: ok next — who owns the rollback runbook and the playbook?
[05:10] Alex Chen: Redwood will provide the playbook; Verity will own the on-call escalation. we'll put both in the shared drive.
[05:17] Rachel Kim: timeline — if we get pinned config this week and tests next week, can we be production-ready by mid-July?
[05:24] Alex Chen: yes that fits our expected rollout path as long as VPC peering and security checks go smoothly.
[05:29] Lisa Gomez: I'll coordinate peering windows with infra.
[05:33] Priya Nair: quick note — competitors were mentioned during internal review; you asked about Anthropic and OpenAI. functionally we'll support similar routing, but our differentiator here is cost/reliability controls and the model catalog with rollout tooling.
[05:48] Samir Patel: good.
[05:50] Alex Chen: ok to recap — Prio items: Priya runs the 2k tests and shares logs by Fri, Alex sends pinned config + playbook by Wed, Samir drops prompts by Thu, Lisa confirms peering window by end of next week. We'll schedule a security deep-dive for the week of Jun 30. Anything else?
[06:09] Rachel Kim: nothing else from me. thanks.
[06:12] Lisa Gomez: thanks all.
[06:13] Priya Nair: thanks — I'll follow up in the doc with batch tuning and the canary policy.
[06:18] Alex Chen: great, meeting adjourned.
[06:20] 
Notes: transcription includes some misheard model names (rw-instruct vs redwood-instruct-v2). Links shared in chat: spreadsheet: https://drive.google.com/verity-poc-perf, pinned-config (to be uploaded), security docs link (to be added).
